incumbent.text: Reproduce-then-boundary-containment: first reproduce the flaw against a live local handler using a fixture root with a sibling marker file and raw requests carrying literal parent-directory segments, so no client-side normalization hides the behavior. Characterize which shapes leak, including the extensionless index-append branch and deep traversal. Then implement the minimal repair at the path-derivation boundary: after joining, resolve the configured root and the joined target and accept only when the target equals the root or begins with the root plus the path separator; otherwise return the existing 404 page. Close with a regression suite covering ordinary files, nested files, directory index, missing files, and traversal variants. Assumption: the join is the single trust boundary; falsifier: a leaking shape that a resolved-prefix check still admits.

hint: The target is a generic HTTP static-file handler that joins the configured content root with the request pathname, appends a default index filename when the joined target has no extension, and streams the target if it exists as a regular file. A pre-fix run on a disposable fixture confirmed five leaking shapes: single parent traversal to a sibling file, deep traversal, doubled-slash traversal, and two extensionless traversal targets served through a sibling directory's index file. Controls behaved normally: root index, ordinary file, and nested file returned 200; missing path and extensionless in-root directory without an index returned 404. Percent-encoded variants were inert because the URL parser did not decode the pathname. The patched and vulnerable trees are separate disposable copies. The observer may read and run both, write fixture trees, and use ephemeral loopback ports. The next action is to add a containment gate immediately after the join and before the index append: resolve the configured root and the joined target, accept only a target equal to the root or beginning with the root plus the path separator, and otherwise return the existing 404 page.
